This includes people, tools, budget, and time.</p></li><li><p><b>Assess resource availability.</b> Check who and what is available. id="resource-management-plan-how-to-create-one-template">Resource management plan: How to create one + template</h2><p data-optly-id="1f71cfef83">As a leader, it can be tough to keep your team from feeling overworked or underused. It's easy to lose track of everyone's workload. This is where resource management helps.</p><p data-optly-id="1335471060">A resource management plan helps you keep track of your team's workload and balance resources. It gives you a clear view of how your team will reach its goals. In this guide, you'll learn what resource management is, how to create a plan, and which tools and techniques can help you manage your team's resources confidently.</p><h2 id="what-is-resource-management">What is resource management?</h2><p data-optly-id="aaedb23f81">Resource management means planning, scheduling, and assigning your team's resources so every project finishes on time and within budget. Resources can be anything that helps you complete a project, like team members, money, equipment, or software.</p><p data-optly-id="a6940e4a0f">When you're deciding how to manage or assign your team's resources, consider a few questions:</p><p></p><ul><li><p data-optly-id="db89861571"><b>What is the availability of each resource?</b></p></li><li><p data-optly-id="f80ac36b84"><b>What are the timelines for each activity?</b></p></li><li><p data-optly-id="21787a223c"><b>How many resources will be required to accomplish each activity?</b></p></li><li><p data-optly-id="d1753c9879"><b>Who is the best person to accomplish the activity effectively?</b></p></li></ul><p></p><p data-optly-id="31b32d71ab">Effectively managing your resources ensures every project is well-equipped and every team member is appropriately allocated, paving the way for successful project completion.</p><h2 id="what-is-a-resource-management-plan">What is a resource management plan?</h2><p data-optly-id="b1f83621cb">A resource management plan is a document that outlines how you'll identify, assign, manage, and monitor all the resources needed to complete a project. It covers human, financial, technical, and physical resources, along with the activities and timelines required to put them to work.</p><p data-optly-id="4eb56785c6">A well-built resource management plan helps you answer key questions like:</p><p></p><ul><li><p data-optly-id="ae539ba6c8"><b>What resources does this project require, and when?</b></p></li><li><p data-optly-id="d69bfa52f3"><b>Who is available, and what skills do they bring?</b></p></li><li><p data-optly-id="c9c02b1d32"><b>How will you handle resource conflicts or shortages?</b></p></li><li><p data-optly-id="3d7bd89f4e"><b>What's the budget, and how will funds be distributed?</b></p></li></ul><p></p><p data-optly-id="46057f0fb9">Without this plan, projects can go over budget, team members can become overloaded, and critical tasks can fall through the cracks.</p><h2 id="why-is-resource-management-important">Why is resource management important?</h2><p data-optly-id="792cd67aaa">Resource management helps ensure your team members are confident about the amount of work on their plate and equipped with the tools they need to accomplish each task. underutilized.</p></li><li><p data-optly-id="93b2374dcf">Spot potential resourcing issues in real time and adjust accordingly, preventing staffing issues from affecting project progress.</p></li><li><p data-optly-id="5180a77008">Give your team clarity about their responsibilities and those of their team members, limiting misunderstandings and promoting accountability.</p></li><li><p data-optly-id="d2ef1f9453">Set realistic <a class="ehhoor84 css-uwuh58-link-2-inline-regular" href="/features/goals-reporting/goals">project goals</a>, reducing the likelihood of missing important milestones and increasing the chances of on-time project completion.</p></li><li><p data-optly-id="39a11d93c6">Enhance your team's profitability by optimizing resource utilization, improving <a class="ehhoor84 css-uwuh58-link-2-inline-regular" href="/resources/operational-efficiency">operational efficiency</a>, and ensuring projects are completed within budget.</p></li><li><p data-optly-id="42d1aabb91">Improve future resource planning by leveraging knowledge gained to better estimate and forecast bandwidth for upcoming projects.</p></li></ul><p></p><h3 id="impact-of-poor-resource-planning">Impact of poor resource planning</h3><p data-optly-id="928d26057a">When resource planning is mishandled, the ripple effects can undermine even the most well-intentioned projects. Here are some common consequences of inadequate resource management:</p><p></p><ul><li><p data-optly-id="a720f29c3b">Increased workloads can lead to team members <a class="ehhoor84 css-uwuh58-link-2-inline-regular" href="/resources/quartz-burnout-guide">experiencing burnout</a>.</p></li><li><p data-optly-id="f6b273e7d0">Poor resource allocation results in underutilized skills and wasted potential.</p></li><li><p data-optly-id="1747728493">Relying on spreadsheets rather than a resource management program creates bottlenecks and complicates decision-making.</p></li><li><p data-optly-id="2bcc1c058c">Lack of real-time resource forecasting makes it difficult to anticipate shortages.</p></li><li><p data-optly-id="80f540387a">Inadequate capacity planning can cause overallocation, delaying project timelines.</p></li><li><p data-optly-id="19256c4375">Without effective resource leveling, projects may face unexpected delays and increased costs.</p></li><li><p data-optly-id="3d83ed76fc">Insufficient resource management negatively affects profitability and stakeholder satisfaction.</p></li></ul><p></p><p data-optly-id="8cfcc381ab">Ultimately, managing resources in a team is essential for optimizing workflows, improving project execution, and ensuring the success of future initiatives.</p><h2 id="what-should-a-resource-management-plan-include">What should a resource management plan include?</h2><p data-optly-id="6aa08e0501">Every resource management plan should include a list of required resources, defined roles and responsibilities, a resource schedule, acquisition methods, and documented assumptions and constraints. The specifics will vary by project, but here are the core components to cover:</p><p></p><ul><li><p data-optly-id="942e59ae7b"><b>Resource requirements:</b> List every resource you'll need to complete the project, including team members, equipment, software, and budget. Be specific about quantities and skill sets.</p></li><li><p data-optly-id="13edbd578f"><b>Roles and responsibilities:</b> Define who is responsible for each task or workstream, and clarify who approves resource requests or changes. This helps prevent confusion and keeps accountability clear.</p></li><li><p data-optly-id="3c5a0e13ab"><b>Resource breakdown structure:</b> Organize your resources into categories, such as human, financial, and material, so you can see at a glance how they'll be distributed across the project.</p></li><li><p data-optly-id="f0305141c7"><b>Timeframes and schedules:</b> Map out when each resource is needed, for how long, and at what capacity. Aligning resource availability with your project timeline helps you avoid bottlenecks.</p></li><li><p data-optly-id="d76d077b10"><b>Assumptions and constraints:</b> Document any factors that could affect resourcing, such as team member availability, budget limits, schedule dependencies, or <a class="ehhoor84 css-uwuh58-link-2-inline-regular" href="/resources/scope-management-plan">scope boundaries</a>.</p></li><li><p data-optly-id="ecb3a546db"><b>Resource acquisition methods:</b> Outline how you'll secure the resources you don't already have, whether that means hiring, contracting, purchasing, or reallocating from other projects.</p></li></ul><p></p><p data-optly-id="df94c521b2">By documenting these elements upfront, you give your team and stakeholders a shared reference point that makes it easier to plan, adapt, and stay aligned as the project moves forward.</p><h2 id="resource-management-techniques">Resource management techniques</h2><p data-optly-id="942a6ce58f">Resource management techniques help you find the smartest ways to use your team's skills and resources. Here are four common methods at a glance.</p><p data-optly-id="b332636913"><b>Resource allocation</b></p><ul><li><p data-optly-id="18e91b22c9"><b>What it does:</b> Assigns the best-fit resource to each task based on skills and capacity</p></li><li><p data-optly-id="a89fc31993"><b>When to use it:</b> At project kickoff and during planning</p></li></ul><p data-optly-id="0139ca5127"><b>Resource utilization</b></p><ul><li><p data-optly-id="5fb5901dcc"><b>What it does:</b> Measures how effectively resources are being used</p></li><li><p data-optly-id="b12d186585"><b>When to use it:</b> Ongoing, to balance workloads</p></li></ul><p data-optly-id="5d11b7c274"><b>Resource forecasting</b></p><ul><li><p data-optly-id="fbbf27e5d5"><b>What it does:</b> Predicts future resource needs based on trends and capacity</p></li><li><p data-optly-id="3c281c09af"><b>When to use it:</b> During project planning</p></li></ul><p data-optly-id="5f5d96ec0c"><b>Resource leveling</b></p><ul><li><p data-optly-id="14038738b0"><b>What it does:</b> Redistributes work to resolve shortages or overallocation</p></li><li><p data-optly-id="8ae675eafb"><b>When to use it:</b> When workloads become uneven</p></li></ul><p></p><h3 id="1-resource-allocation">1. Resource allocation</h3><p data-optly-id="c5ee33e781">Resource allocation is the process of assigning the best-fit resource to each task based on your team's skills and capacity. It goes beyond filling slots: the goal is to strategically match your team's strengths to the specific demands of each project.</p><h3 id="4-resource-utilization">4. Resource utilization</h3><p data-optly-id="5710f51369">Resource utilization involves using tools like utilization reports and <a class="ehhoor84 css-uwuh58-link-2-inline-regular" href="/features/resource-management/time-tracking">time tracking software</a> to identify your team's capacity over a specific period of time. It's a capacity-planning technique that helps you identify whether project resources are underutilized or overallocated, so you can better manage workloads.</p><h3 id="5-resource-forecasting">5. Resource forecasting</h3><p data-optly-id="ffa17c7c31">Resource forecasting involves predicting what resources you'll need for future projects and initiatives. By analyzing past trends, project metrics, and your team's current capacity during the <a class="ehhoor84 css-uwuh58-link-2-inline-regular" href="/resources/project-management-plan">project planning stage</a>, you can spot potential bottlenecks and support better <a class="ehhoor84 css-uwuh58-link-2-inline-regular" href="/resources/project-risk-management-process">risk management</a> before they affect your timeline.</p><h3 id="6-resource-leveling">6. Resource leveling</h3><p data-optly-id="b4ccab811f"><a class="ehhoor84 css-uwuh58-link-2-inline-regular" href="/resources/resource-leveling">Resource leveling</a> is a resource management solution designed to combat shortages or overallocation by using underutilized resources. For example, this might mean shifting work from one team member's plate to another who has similar skills and additional capacity. Or, it could mean taking advantage of skill sets that typically aren't utilized, like having a website content writer create social copy.</p><h2 id="types-of-resource-management">Types of resource management</h2><p data-optly-id="7357b2d67a">Effective resource management is key to steering any organization toward its goals. Here, we focus on three fundamental types of resources: human, financial, and material. Each category plays a unique role in the broader spectrum of resource planning and is a crucial component of any resource management plan.</p><h3 id="human-resource-management-work-resources">Human resource management (work resources)</h3><p data-optly-id="8be93350ee"><a class="ehhoor84 css-uwuh58-link-2-inline-regular" href="/resources/resource-management-plan">Human resource management</a> is the strategic approach to managing a company's most valuable assets, its employees. This involves not just recruiting and hiring but also integrating workflow and automation tools to streamline training, performance assessments, and career development planning.</p><p></p><ul><li><p data-optly-id="693932917a"><b>Example:</b> A software company might enhance its human resource management by using workflow automation to efficiently align its workforce with emerging technology trends. This ensures that developers are systematically trained in the latest programming languages and Agile methodologies. By automating parts of the training and development process, the company can quickly adapt to changes in the fast-paced tech industry.</p></li></ul><p></p><h3 id="financial-resource-management-cost-resources">Financial resource management (cost resources)</h3><p data-optly-id="846e23c22a">Financial resource management is the process of planning, organizing, directing, and controlling financial activities such as procurement and utilization of funds. It involves making informed decisions about allocating financial resources across projects or departments.</p><p></p><ul><li><p data-optly-id="371f23237c"><b>Example:</b> Consider a multinational corporation that allocates budgets across different regions, taking into account local market conditions, operational costs, pricing strategies, and revenue projections. This strategic financial management helps ensure high-priority initiatives receive the funding and resources they need to thrive. These resources, such as consulting or other professional services, are tactical spending that is helpful but not the main purpose of budgetary allocation.</p></li></ul><p></p><h3 id="material-resource-management-material-assets">Material resource management (material assets)</h3><p data-optly-id="57e7e000cd">Material resource management involves the efficient planning, sourcing, and utilization of physical resources required for <a class="ehhoor84 css-uwuh58-link-2-inline-regular" href="/resources/operations-management">business operations</a>. It encompasses inventory management, purchasing, and supply chain optimization to support the entire project lifecycle, from initial planning to final delivery.</p><p data-optly-id="36b83151dd">By adopting an <a class="ehhoor84 css-uwuh58-link-2-inline-regular" href="/templates/inventory">inventory template</a>, businesses can align their material resources with project timelines, thereby reducing costly delays. Furthermore, implementing <a class="ehhoor84 css-uwuh58-link-2-inline-regular" href="/resources/inventory-management-software">inventory management software</a> is key in this process because it offers real-time visibility and control over material resources.</p><p></p><ul><li><p data-optly-id="d2891b74b1"><b>Example:</b> A manufacturing firm may use material resource management to ensure a steady supply of raw materials, such as metals and plastics. By doing so, the firm can avoid production delays and cost overruns, thereby maintaining product quality and meeting customer delivery timelines.</p></li></ul><p></p><h2 id="how-to-create-a-resource-management-plan">How to create a resource management plan</h2><p data-optly-id="7c2245da7a">Creating a comprehensive resource management plan is essential for any organization looking to optimize its resources effectively. This plan involves a series of steps that ensure resources are deployed efficiently and comply with both the <a class="ehhoor84 css-uwuh58-link-2-inline-regular" href="/resources/project-management-phases">project lifecycle</a> and overarching business goals.</p><p data-optly-id="046bd6ec12">Below are the five key steps in developing a solid resource management plan.</p><h3 id="step-1-resource-planning-and-budgeting">Step 1: Resource planning and budgeting</h3><p data-optly-id="927849ac8f">The first step in creating a resource management plan involves detailed resource planning and budgeting. This process includes forecasting resource needs and matching them to the available budget.</p><p></p><p data-optly-id="4e86b33010"><b>Example:</b> A tech startup, XYZ Software, begins its journey by planning resources for its innovative project management software. They forecast the demand for qualified software engineers and marketers, set aside money for cloud infrastructure, and make sure their financial resources are distributed effectively between development and marketing.</p><p></p><h3 id="step-2-identify-resources-capacity-planning">Step 2: Identify resources (capacity planning)</h3><p data-optly-id="4df7e385ea">Identifying the right resources is make-or-break for any project's success. This step, often referred to as <a class="ehhoor84 css-uwuh58-link-2-inline-regular" href="/resources/capacity-planning">capacity planning</a>, involves understanding your workforce's availability and skills, as well as the physical and financial resources at your disposal. It's about matching the right resources to the right tasks, ensuring that your human, financial, and material resources align with your project's needs.</p><p></p><ul><li><p data-optly-id="0c55e65a46"><b>Example:</b> XYZ Software conducts a thorough analysis of its team's skills and identifies the need for additional software engineers with expertise in cloud computing. The company also assesses its current financial resources to ensure sufficient funding is available for these new hires.</p></li></ul><p></p><h3 id="step-3-allocate-resources">Step 3: Allocate resources</h3><p data-optly-id="2174b04961">Once resources are identified, the next step is effective allocation. This involves assigning resources to various tasks and projects based on their availability and suitability. <a class="ehhoor84 css-uwuh58-link-2-inline-regular" href="/resources/resource-allocation">Resource allocation</a> ensures that every project gets the necessary resources without overburdening any single aspect of the business.</p><p></p><ul><li><p data-optly-id="a80d302821"><b>Example:</b> XYZ Software assigns its existing team to the initial development phases, while the newly hired cloud experts build the cloud infrastructure. Financial resources are allocated to ensure both teams have the necessary tools and software licenses.</p></li></ul><p></p><h3 id="step-4-resource-tracking">Step 4: Resource tracking</h3><p data-optly-id="b1ff340198">Tracking resources throughout the project lifecycle ensures everything is proceeding as planned. By monitoring usage and comparing it against requirements, you can identify shortages or surpluses early and make timely adjustments.</p><p></p><ul><li><p data-optly-id="d9c1a2ccce"><b>Example:</b> As XYZ Software's project progresses, they use project management software to track the time and resources spent on each aspect of the project. By doing so, they are able to make adjustments in real time by identifying areas where resources might be over- or underutilized.</p></li></ul><p></p><h3 id="step-5-resource-optimization">Step 5: Resource optimization</h3><p data-optly-id="ab41f561b8">The final step in the resource management plan is optimization. This involves analyzing resource performance and usage, and making necessary adjustments to improve efficiency.</p><p data-optly-id="af51a0805c">Resource optimization might include implementing automation tools to streamline processes or revising strategies based on performance data. The aim is to use resources as efficiently as possible, which will help the organization succeed as a whole.</p><p></p><ul><li><p data-optly-id="36d4a04492"><b>Example:</b> After launching the first version of their software, XYZ Software reviews their resource usage data. They realize that automating certain testing processes can free up developer time. This enables the team to focus more on critical tasks, thereby optimizing their use of human resources for future updates.</p></li></ul><p></p><h2 id="how-to-manage-resources-effectively">How to manage resources effectively</h2><p data-optly-id="3330f0a42e">Moving from theory to action doesn't have to be overwhelming. These ten best practices will help you streamline resource allocation, balance workloads, and set your team up for project success.</p><p></p><ol><li><p data-optly-id="7f236e90b5"><b>Use a </b><a class="ehhoor84 css-uwuh58-link-2-inline-regular" href="/resources/introduction-to-work-management"><b>work management platform</b></a> to streamline the planning process and ensure consistent, efficient allocation of resources across projects. While traditional resource management tools, like Gantt charts or spreadsheets, are useful ways to track capacity, their limited scope can't match the extensive capabilities offered by a comprehensive work management platform.</p></li><li><p data-optly-id="0951dd508e"><b>Measure available resources</b> by gauging team capacity and necessary tools. This will help you ensure realistic resource allocation and avoid rescheduling issues.</p></li><li><p data-optly-id="e4385425ad"><b>Set start and end dates</b> so you get a realistic timeframe for how long each task will take and set realistic expectations for your team.</p></li><li><p data-optly-id="7c7b581397"><b>Know your employees'skill sets</b> so you can determine the best resourcing for each task.</p></li><li><p data-optly-id="b45ae16a27"><b>Set accessible project goals</b> to help you prioritize your team's work and drive high-impact work forward.</p></li><li><p data-optly-id="21738dfa25"><b>Help your team increase their</b> <a class="ehhoor84 css-uwuh58-link-2-inline-regular" href="/resources/utilization-rate"><b>utilization rate</b></a> by automating routine, low-impact tasks so your team can focus on actionable, strategic, and billable work.</p></li><li><p data-optly-id="f88ef6b683"><b>Adjust resources as necessary</b> because tasks, project timelines, and priorities change.</p></li><li><p data-optly-id="470b572740"><b>Keep some team bandwidth open</b> for new work or priorities that might come up.</p></li><li><p data-optly-id="596072b716"><b>Check in on your team</b> to ensure each team member feels their work volume is fair and achievable.</p></li><li><p data-optly-id="40a2d92b0f"><b>Connect your resource management plan to your</b> <a class="ehhoor84 css-uwuh58-link-2-inline-regular" href="/resources/operational-planning"><b>operational plan</b></a> in order to effectively manage your team's time and align daily tasks with <a class="ehhoor84 css-uwuh58-link-2-inline-regular" href="/resources/strategic-planning">strategic goals</a>.</p></li></ol><p></p><h2 id="how-to-choose-the-best-resource-management-software">How to choose the best resource management software</h2><p data-optly-id="8542ad0d43">With so many resource management software choices, picking the right one can be tough. Here are some tips to help you choose a tool that fits your team's needs and improves how you manage resources:</p><p></p><ul><li><p data-optly-id="eb3e5aa60e"><b>Identify your needs:</b> Start by outlining what you require from a resource management solution, such as resource allocation, capacity planning, and real-time tracking. Knowing your priorities will help narrow down the options.</p></li><li><p data-optly-id="1f7193ff67"><b>Seek seamless integrations</b>: Choose software that integrates smoothly with your existing tools, such as portfolio management platforms, time-tracking systems, and communication apps. For example, <a class="ehhoor84 css-uwuh58-link-2-inline-regular" href="/apps?category=all-apps">Asana offers robust integrations</a> with Microsoft Teams, Google Workspace, and other essential platforms.</p></li><li><p data-optly-id="b9d7dca037"><b>Prioritize ease of use:</b> Choose software with a simple interface so your team can start using it quickly. Look for easy navigation and dashboards that make managing resources simple for everyone.</p></li><li><p data-optly-id="2766c3d7ed"><b>Make sure th</b>e software can grow with your business. Whether your team gets bigger or you take on more projects, the tool should handle more work without slowing down.</p></li><li><p data-optly-id="2b011892e6"><b>Use automation:</b> Features like automated scheduling and reporting can help you use resources better by taking care of routine tasks.</p></li><li><p data-optly-id="5166dbab26"><b>Compare pricing:</b> Look at different plans to find one that fits your budget and has the features you need. Think about how much value the software will add to your resource management.</p></li><li><p data-optly-id="c669f6ac95"><b>Read reviews and request demos:</b> Gain insights from other users by reading reviews and testimonials. Additionally, request demos to see the software in action and determine if it aligns with your expectations and workflows. Tip: Try <a class="ehhoor84 css-uwuh58-link-2-inline-regular" href="/create-account">a free trial of Asana</a> and begin resource planning today.</p></li></ul><p></p><p data-optly-id="6c58e6fceb">To pick the best resource management software, balance features, ease of use, and price.
